title: Lisse extension across the boundary of a smooth curve
statement:
Fix the finite-field datum $k_0=\mathbf F_q$, $k=\overline{k_0}$ and a prime $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}(k_0)$ as in [def-weil-finite-field-fiber]. Let $C_0$ be a smooth geometrically connected separated curve of finite type over $k_0$, let $j_0:U_0\hookrightarrow C_0$ be a dense open immersion, and put $S_0=C_0\setminus U_0$, $C=C_0\times_{k_0}k$ and $U=U_0\times_{k_0}k$. Smoothness is [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms], and curve means pure dimension one [def-weil-pure-dimension]. Let $F$ be a lisse $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$-Weil sheaf on $U_0$, using the adic lisse convention [def-pod-lisse-l-adic-sheaves] and the Weil structure [def-weil-weil-sheaf-complex]. For each $x\in S_0$, let $I_x$ act on the local geometric generic stalk of $F$ by [d-real-boundary].

There exists a lisse Weil sheaf $G$ on $C_0$ together with a Weil-equivariant isomorphism $j_0^*G\simeq F$ if and only if every $I_x$ acts trivially. If these equivalent conditions hold, the ordinary direct image $j_{0*}F$ of [def-wf-middle-extension] is lisse and, for every such pair $(G,\alpha)$, the morphism $G\to j_{0*}F$ adjoint to $\alpha$ is a Weil-equivariant isomorphism. In particular the extension with its specified restriction is unique up to unique isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 0BTD, lemma-normal-pione-quotient-inertia (kernel generated by inertia), with the adic fibre equivalence of cor-galois-lisse-representations; Weil II (1.1.12) for Weil descent. The affine-line specialization is in rem-dl-a1-conventions, second paragraph.

proof.text: By [prop-wf-weil-sheaf-representation-equivalence], the lisse Weil sheaf F on U_0 corresponds to its geometric generic stalk V=F_{\bar\eta} with a continuous Weil-group representation \rho_U:W(U_0)\to\operatorname{Aut}(V). The local inertia action at each x\in S_0 is the restriction of this representation to the subgroup I_x specified by [d-real-boundary].

source.place: Second paragraph, equivalence between extension to a lisse sheaf and trivial inertia

proof.text: By [lem-dl-a1-weil-kernel-inertia], the kernel K of the restriction map r:W(U_0)\to W(C_0) is the smallest closed normal subgroup of W(U_0) containing the images of the I_x. If every I_x acts trivially on V, then \ker\rho_U is a closed normal subgroup (\rho_U is continuous and \operatorname{Aut}(V) is Hausdorff) containing every image of I_x, hence contains K; conversely K contains the images of the I_x, so \rho_U(K)=1 forces every I_x to act trivially. By part (2) of [lem-wf-dense-open-pi1-surjective], r is surjective and preserves degrees. Hence a representation killing K factors uniquely as \rho_U=\rho_C\circ r for a homomorphism \rho_C of W(C_0). It is continuous because r is open: r is the restriction of the continuous surjection of profinite groups \pi_1(U_0)\to\pi_1(C_0), which is open, and since r preserves degrees the inverse image of W(C_0) is exactly W(U_0), so r(W(U_0)\cap O)=W(C_0)\cap r(O) for every open O; if instead W is topologized with its geometric subgroup open and profinite, r restricts there to the continuous surjection \pi_1(U)\to\pi_1(C) of profinite groups, again open. Conversely a representation of the form \rho_C\circ r kills K and hence every I_x.

source.place: Tag 0BTD, lemma-normal-pione-quotient-inertia, and the quotient criterion

proof.text: Apply [prop-wf-weil-sheaf-representation-equivalence] on C_0 (a curve in the sense of [d-real-setup]: nonempty, separated, smooth, finite type, pure dimension one, with connected C) to the descended W(C_0)-representation \rho_C of Step 2; it gives a lisse Weil sheaf G on C_0 with (G_{\bar\eta},\rho_G)\simeq(V,\rho_C). Take the base point \bar\eta in U. The Weil fundamental representation of j_0^*G is \rho_G\circ r: by [def-wf-fundamental-representation] its stalk is (j_0^*G)_{\bar\eta}=G_{\bar\eta}, the geometric action of \pi_1(U,\bar\eta) on the fibre is through the map \pi_1(U,\bar\eta)\to\pi_1(C,\bar\eta) induced by pullback of finite étale covers (a cover trivializing G pulls back to one trivializing j_0^*G, with the same fibre at \bar\eta), and the Weil structure of j_0^*G is the restriction of that of G, so for a Frobenius lift s\in W(U_0) the operator T_s of j_0^*G is the operator T_{r(s)} of G. Hence j_0^*G and F have isomorphic Weil representations \rho_C\circ r=\rho_U, and the equivalence on U_0 (U_0 is again such a curve, being a nonempty open of C_0 with U a nonempty open of the irreducible C) gives the Weil-equivariant isomorphism \alpha:j_0^*G\simeq F. Conversely, for an extension (G,\alpha) the same computation shows \rho_U\simeq\rho_G\circ r, which kills K, so Step 2 forces every I_x to act trivially.

source.place: Second paragraph, extension criterion and Weil descent

proof.text: Assume the equivalent conditions and choose (G,\alpha). The geometric curve C is connected (C_0 is geometrically connected), Noetherian (finite type over k) and normal by [lem-sc-smooth-normal], since it is a separated smooth finite-type curve over the algebraically closed field k; and U, the inverse image of U_0 in C, is a dense open of C, because C\to C_0 is open (base change to a field is universally open) and U_0 is dense in C_0. Part (3) of [lem-wf-dense-open-pi1-surjective], applied to the underlying lisse sheaf of G on C, says that the adjunction unit G\to j_*j^*G is an isomorphism at every finite coefficient level, hence for the lisse \overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell-sheaf. It is Weil-equivariant: the geometric Frobenius g commutes with j (g_C\circ j=j\circ g_U), the Weil structure of the ordinary direct image j_*F of [def-wf-middle-extension] is the one transported through g_C^*j_*\simeq j_*g_U^* (pullback along the automorphism g), and the unit is natural, hence commutes with these identifications. Composing the unit with j_*\alpha gives the morphism G\to j_*F adjoint to \alpha, an isomorphism of Weil sheaves. Hence j_*F is lisse and the asserted morphism is a Weil-equivariant isomorphism.

source.place: Second paragraph, ordinary direct image and lisse extension

proof.text: If (G,\alpha) and (G\prime,\alpha\prime) are two extensions, the restriction functor on lisse Weil sheaves is fully faithful by part (4) of [lem-wf-dense-open-pi1-surjective], applied to the curve C_0 and its nonempty open U_0. Thus there is a unique morphism G\to G\prime restricting to \alpha^{\prime-1}\circ\alpha, and it is an isomorphism because its restriction is. This proves uniqueness with the specified restriction.

source.place: Second paragraph, uniqueness of the extension

split_report.summary: Audited the imported extension criterion against the smooth-curve conventions. Added one genuine dependency, the kernel description generated by boundary inertia, then rewrote the proof as representation descent, construction and converse, ordinary direct-image recovery, and full-faithfulness uniqueness. No statement clause or hypothesis was changed. Maintainer reader (FIX): step 2 now cites clause (2) of lem-wf-dense-open-pi1-surjective for the surjectivity and writes out openness of r; step 3 writes out why j_0^*G has representation rho_G o r; step 4 uses clause (3) of lem-wf-dense-open-pi1-surjective on the geometric curve C (with lem-sc-smooth-normal) instead of lem-a1-lisse-middle-extension, whose statement is for sheaves on the k_0-curve C_0, and writes out the Weil equivariance of the unit; tool uses declared.
split_report.blueprint: Realizes the second paragraph of rem-dl-a1-conventions: extension to a lisse sheaf over the boundary is equivalent to trivial local inertia, with uniqueness and ordinary direct-image identification.

tool_uses.why: Steps 1 and 3 take the exact equivalence between lisse Weil sheaves on a curve and continuous Weil-group representations on the generic stalk; unit sk-d-dl-a1-setup is a conventions remark citing no unit and no node of it gives this equivalence.

Steps 2, 4 and 5 take clause (2) (surjective degree-preserving Weil restriction), clause (3) (unit N->k_*k^*N is an isomorphism for lisse N on a connected normal Noetherian scheme) and clause (4) (full faithfulness of restriction on curves) as black boxes; no node of the unit gives them.
Step 4 takes normality of the smooth geometric curve C, a hypothesis of clause (3) above; generic tool.

The coefficients are adic Qbar_l Weil pairs. Small cases check out: no boundary point, the Kummer sheaf on G_m, Artin-Schreier at infinity, and a geometrically constant sheaf. lean.statement: theorem lisse_extension_iff_trivial_inertia (D : FiniteFieldDatum.{u}) (l : ℕ) [Fact l.Prime] [Fact (l ≠ D.p)] (c : Scheme.MiddleExtensionCurve D) [GeometricallyConnected c.C.hom] {WU : WeilGroup (c.U.left ↘ Spec (.of D.k₀))} {WC : WeilGroup (c.C.left ↘ Spec (.of D.k₀))} (b : BoundaryDatum c.j.left WU WC) (M : LisseMonodromy l (c.U.left ↘ Spec (.of D.k₀)).geometricFiber D.k₀) (B : WeilGroup.BasePointData WU) (hM : M.IsEquivalenceAt B.t) (F : WeilSheaf D.k₀ l c.U.left) (hF : F.IsLisse) : ((∃ G : WeilSheaf D.k₀ l c.C.left, G.IsLisse ∧ Nonempty ((WeilSheaf.upperStar c.j.left).obj G ≅ F)) ↔ ∀ (x : ↥((Set.range c.j.left.base)ᶜ)) (g : b.inertia x) (v : LisseMonodromy.StalkSpace B.t (F.toLisse hF)), WeilGroup.canonicalFundamentalRep M B F hF g.1 v = v) ∧ ((∀ (x : ↥((Set.range c.j.left.base)ᶜ)) (g : b.inertia x) (v : LisseMonodromy.StalkSpace B.t (F.toLisse hF)), WeilGroup.canonicalFundamentalRep M B F hF g.1 v = v) → ((curveWeilMiddleExtension c.j.left).obj F).IsLisse ∧ (∀ (G : WeilSheaf D.k₀ l c.C.left), G.IsLisse → ∀ α : (WeilSheaf.upperStar c.j.left).obj G ≅ F, ∃ e : G ≅ (curveWeilMiddleExtension c.j.left).obj F, e.hom.hom.hom.f = (adicUpperStarLowerStarAdjunction l (Scheme.Hom.geometricFiberMap c.j.left (comp_over c.j.left (Spec (.of D.k₀))))).homEquiv G.carrier F.carrier α.hom.hom.hom.f) ∧ (∀ (G G' : WeilSheaf D.k₀ l c.C.left), G.IsLisse → G'.IsLisse → ∀ (α : (WeilSheaf.upperStar c.j.left).obj G ≅ F) (α' : (WeilSheaf.upperStar c.j.left).obj G' ≅ F), ∃! e : G ≅ G', (WeilSheaf.upperStar c.j.left).map e.hom ≫ α'.hom = α.hom))
